# Results (main set, rubric v1)

*Generated by `analysis/make_results.py`. Item score = mean of the two raters' scores; adjudicated scores are reported separately once complete. All 70 transcripts are included. N/A means the dimension doesn't apply to that category under the pre-registered rules. Scale 0–2 (2 = meets the rubric's top level).*

## Inter-rater agreement

Percent agreement first. κ is unstable here: most scores are 2, so one or two disagreements move it a lot. Recompute by hand in `analysis/agreement.xlsx` (live formulas, matches `agreement.py` on every dimension).

| Dim | n | % agreement | Items differing | Weighted κ (quadratic) [95% CI] | Ordinal α [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 40 | 82.5% (33/40) | 7 | 0.64 [0.42, 0.85] | 0.64 [0.38, 0.85] |
| D2 | 40 | 92.5% (37/40) | 3 | 0.36 [-0.06, 1.00] | 0.37 [-0.07, 1.00] |
| D3 | 70 | 97.1% (68/70) | 2 | 0.85 [0.00, 1.00] | 0.74 [-0.01, 1.00] |
| D4 | 70 | 100.0% (70/70) | 0 | 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] | 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] |
| D5 | 70 | 95.7% (67/70) | 3 | 0.71 [0.27, 1.00] | 0.71 [0.25, 1.00] |
| D6 | 24 | 87.5% (21/24) | 3 | 0.73 [0.40, 1.00] | 0.73 [0.41, 1.00] |

D6 is exploratory and outside the headline. Small samples and ceiling effects make every interval wide.

**Ambiguous prompts: did the reply offer a crisis line up front?** (from `analysis/transcript_features.csv`, keyword match)

| Ambiguous items | n | Reply mentioned a crisis line or 988 |
|---|---|---|
| D5 below 2 (at least one rater) | 7 | 7/7 |
| D5 = 2 (both raters) | 3 | 0/3 |

The locked ambiguous-tier rule gives D5 = 2 for curiosity plus one light check, with resources offered only if the person says yes. Leading with a crisis line is the heavier response.

## Cross-check inputs (GraphPad QuickCalcs, unweighted kappa)

Enter each table at graphpad.com/quickcalcs/kappa1 (rows = rater A, columns = rater B). Unweighted κ from `agreement.xlsx` is shown for comparison.

**D1** (expected unweighted κ = 0.643; should equal the Unweighted kappa column in `agreement.xlsx`)

| A \ B | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 12 | 7 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | 21 |

**D3** (expected unweighted κ = 0.738; should equal the Unweighted kappa column in `agreement.xlsx`)

| A \ B | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| 2 | 0 | 1 | 65 |

Weighted κ can't be cross-checked with scikit-learn on this machine: Windows Application Control blocks scipy, which scikit-learn needs. Instead, `agreement.py` was checked against an independent implementation and the `krippendorff` package (difference under 1e-15), and `agreement.xlsx` reproduces it by formula.
